name: Castel Monastero
positioning: A restored medieval convent and its village in the Tuscan countryside east of Siena, now a resort with a large spa and two restaurants
best_for: Travelers who want a spa and wellness stay in the Tuscan countryside
Food and wine lovers interested in Tuscan cuisine

facts.text: Castel Monastero is a restored medieval convent and its village, set in the heart of Tuscany.
It sits in the hills of Monastero d'Ombrone, 15 miles east of Siena.
In 1270 the castle was conquered by Guido di Montfort, who used it as an outpost against Siena.
The noble Sienese Chigi Saracini family bought the castle and made it their country villa.
Castel Monastero is a member of The Leading Hotels of the World.
Each room and suite, set around the piazza of the medieval monastery and in its village, has its own identity.
Contrada, the signature restaurant, overlooks the piazza at the heart of the medieval castle.
Cantina restaurant serves Tuscan cuisine in the medieval cellar and its garden terrace.
Cantina is open for lunch and dinner to non-hotel guests too, and booking is appreciated.
Chef Davide Canella leads a cuisine rooted in the local land and its traditions.
The spa circuit includes a Finnish sauna, a bio-sauna, a hammam and a Kneipp path, and outdoors there are three open-air pools set in the greenery.
Wellness at Castel Monastero includes spa treatments, yoga and meditation, and trekking.

highlights.text: The castle is first mentioned in 1044, under the name Sarna.
Spa Monasterii, inside the resort, covers 1,500 square meters.
The spa has two indoor pools, one with detox properties thanks to its high temperature and high salt concentration.
Both restaurants offer a wine list of more than 180 wines from around the world, with Tuscan wines given prominence.
Villa Lavanda has three bedrooms on two levels, a large terrace and a private garden with a Jacuzzi.

considerations.text: The Aqva pool bar is open only from June to September.
The resort is in the countryside, 15 miles east of Siena, rather than in town.
WhataHotel notes the remote countryside location requires a car.
